title: Bands heard when young; the two Ambroses and the cheese-box banjo
summary: Glass says he loved all the older bands, distinguishes two Ambroses (banjo and trombone), and describes a banjo made from a cheese box.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Bill, did you get who some of the people you heard when he was young? We asked a few.

Yeah, who were some of the bands you heard when you just were getting interested in music? Do you remember the name of some of the bands? When you were quite young, you know, some of the musicians you liked?

Well I liked a lot of them. I liked all the bands. Because I just was wild over the music. I liked Ambrose and all them fellas like that, and it was all older bands than me. And I just come up with them. Ambrose was a banjo player? Yeah, Ambrose was all in me when I started playing. Ambrose what?
Ambrose, he used to play banjo. I got him confused.
Now is it Ambrose that played trombone? Ambrose played trombone.

He played trombone and one played banjo. Ambrose made him a banjo, he had a banjo made out of one of them cheese box. He'd make his banjo. Who did he play with? Well he was playing with Johnny Predos and them. Wooden Joe. Well they just would move around.
But he would play that funny little banjo, that homemade banjo on a real band? Yeah, on a real band.

He made it. It was made. I didn't know if I could get my hand on it. I'm going to find out from some of these people that they got that banjo. It's made out of cheese box. He glued that and made it and put heads on it. It was a banjo too. I'd love to see it. You could hear that baby, you could hear that baby. Yeah, he made it. Now just like Noone had made that horn, he used to slide. Kazooka. That kazooka, he was made there.
